item.description:
Note Ferry 2.1 makes getting started, editing, and recovering from errors feel more at home on your Mac.
- **An editing interface with room to work.** Softly shaded text fields separate editable text from the result. Clear, the summarizer picker, Format only, and the primary action stay in a fixed bar at the bottom of the window. - **A welcome you can revisit.** Start with local formatting or set up a summarizer. Run Setup Again in Settings walks through the same flow without clearing saved connections or preferences. Claude keys are masked by default, and setup only shows controls for your selected provider. - **More control over clarification.** Skip a pending question check with Summarize now, continue without questions if that check fails, and review submitted answers with Answers… during an interview. Keep the interview preference in Settings. - **Clearer recovery and results.** Errors offer relevant recovery actions. Failed follow-ups keep your submitted answers accessible, and Retry connection rechecks a saved Claude key without another paste. Results keep context collapsed until you need it; processing details and reported usage are available from the information button. - **Familiar Mac behavior.** Standard File, Edit, Window, and Help commands, Redo, keyboard shortcuts, saved window size, and scrolling Settings content make the app easier to use with a keyboard or a smaller window.
Format only still runs locally without AI. Note Ferry protects newer clipboard content and never creates or edits an Apple Note. Review important details in AI-generated summaries.
Version 2.1 is build 13. The universal app supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs and requires macOS 14 or later. Apple Intelligence requires a compatible Mac running macOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled. Runtime testing has been on Apple silicon with macOS 27; Intel hardware and older macOS versions remain untested.

Note Ferry 2.0 helps clear up confusing details before they become notes.
- **Clarify before summarizing.** Your selected model reviews the text in the background and asks questions only when an answer could materially improve the summary. Questions include verified source excerpts when useful. Choose a radio-button answer, select Something else to write your own, or leave questions unanswered and finish the summary. - **Keep control of the interview.** Continue through useful follow-ups or choose Finish & summarize at any point. The interview is on by default; turn off Ask clarifying questions before summarizing in Settings to skip the extra processing. Interviews use additional tokens and time, and Claude API requests can cost more. - **Provide context once.** Add names, terminology, or background separately from the source. Context and your interview answers stay visible under Context used, with their own copy action, without being appended to Copy summary. - **A clearer interface.** Summarize & format is now the primary action on the left. Larger, resizable windows fit the available screen, excerpts sit beside their questions with readable spacing, and visible scrollbars show where more content is available. Tab moves through answers, arrow keys change radio choices, and Command-Return continues the interview. - **See reported usage.** Results include elapsed summary time and provider-reported token counts, including interview requests when available. Apple Intelligence token reporting requires macOS 27. Missing or cancelled usage is shown as unavailable rather than as a complete total.
Format only still runs locally without AI. The app does not keep a transcript library, edit Apple Notes, or silently switch providers. The clipboard remains unchanged during the interview, and anything you copy while processing is protected when the summary finishes.
Version 2.0 is build 11. The universal app supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs and requires macOS 14 or later. Apple Intelligence requires a compatible Mac running macOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled. Its smaller context budget may require shorter interview answers or an earlier finish. Review important details in any AI-generated summary.

Note Ferry 1.2.5 improves Codex setup for different installations and account types.
- Note Ferry no longer forces a Sol model. Codex chooses its default, or you can enter a model ID available to your account in **Settings → Codex model**. - Codex installed through npm or nvm can now be found even when Terminal has a different PATH from the app. - npm installations keep their Node.js runtime available when Note Ferry starts Codex, including installations in folders with spaces and symlinked launchers. - A missing Node.js runtime now shows a specific setup message instead of reporting that Codex is missing.
Version 1.2.5 is build 10. The universal app supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs and requires macOS 14 or later. **Format only** still runs locally without AI.

Note Ferry 1.2.4 fixes bold formatting around Markdown line breaks.
- Bold headings in numbered lists now paste into Apple Notes without visible `**` markers when followed by a Markdown hard line break. - Emphasis spanning a line break keeps its formatting, while list numbering, links, and inline code are preserved.
Version 1.2.4 is build 9. **Format only** still runs locally without AI.

Note Ferry 1.2.3 makes Claude API key setup easier to finish.
- Paste a key directly into Settings, or choose **Paste from clipboard** to save and check it in one step. - Keys that work across workspaces can use a selected workspace. If Note Ferry needs a workspace ID, the key stays saved while you add it. - Key entry uses a regular text field, and saving leaves the clipboard unchanged. - Connection and setup messages are shorter and more specific.
Version 1.2.3 is build 8. **Format only** still runs locally without AI.

Note Ferry 1.2.2 fixes spacing when you use **Format only** on plain text.
- Questions or complete sentences entered on separate lines now become separate, spaced paragraphs instead of running together. - Line breaks within an unfinished sentence remain line breaks. - Markdown documents continue to use Markdown soft-wrap rules.
Version 1.2.2 is build 7. **Format only** still runs locally without AI.

Note Ferry 1.2.1 improves formatting for text pasted into Apple Notes.
- **Preserve table grids.** Markdown tables keep their rows, columns, headers, and wrapped cell text in the preview and rich clipboard output, including tables copied from ChatGPT Meetings. - **Keep bullet wrapping aligned.** Copying selected text from the formatted preview now preserves native list formatting, so wrapped lines align with the item text after pasting into Notes. - **Format meeting action prompts.** ChatGPT Meetings' `codex-prompt` blocks become readable action-item bullets, including when the source is wrapped in an extra code fence. - **Handle more Markdown patterns.** Improved support for nested lists, checklist symbols, quotes, divider lines, alternate heading syntax, image descriptions, and line breaks. Checklist symbols remain text; select the items and use Notes' Checklist button to make them clickable. - **Use a consistent Codex model.** Codex summaries explicitly use GPT-5.6 Sol with medium reasoning effort rather than the installed CLI's default. Your Codex account and CLI must support that model; Note Ferry does not silently switch models if it is unavailable. Unavailable models now show a specific message instead of a generic connection failure.
### Install or update
Choose **Note Ferry → Check for Updates…**, or download **Note-Ferry-1.2.1-universal.zip**, unzip it, and move **Note Ferry.app** to Applications, replacing the previous copy.
Version 1.2.1 is build 6. The universal app supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs and requires macOS 14 or later. Apple Intelligence needs macOS 26 or later and compatible hardware. Runtime testing has been on Apple silicon with macOS 27; Intel hardware and older macOS versions have not been tested. **Format only** continues to run locally without AI.

Note Ferry 1.2 adds a choice of summarizers: Apple Intelligence on compatible Macs, your signed-in Codex account, or a separately billed Claude API key. A first-run screen chooses the default; the picker beside Summarize & format changes it for one text. Format only still runs locally without AI.
Apple Intelligence is the initial choice on a new install and remains experimental. Review names, attribution, and follow-ups, especially in long transcripts. Claude keys are stored in this Mac's Keychain and sent only after a first-use confirmation.

Note Ferry 1.1 adds in-app update checks through Sparkle. You can choose Check for Updates from the Note Ferry menu. On the second launch, the app asks whether it may check automatically in the background.
The rest of the app still formats text locally or summarizes it with your Codex account when you choose that action.
